simple.meaning: סַחַר (çachar) is a Hebrew word meaning “profit (from trade).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סַחַר (H5504) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Proverbs 3:14, with occurrences in Proverbs, Isaiah.

simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in סַחַר (H5504) before moving outward to related references.

firstOccurrence.englishText: For her good profit is better than getting silver,

timeline.evidenceText: For her good profit is better than getting silver,
She perceives that her merchandise is profitable.

Her merchandise and her wages will be holiness to Yahweh. It will not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise will be for those who dwell before Yahweh, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing.
